task_2.title: Preserve root causes for unsupported JWT algorithms
task_2.description: Version 2.3.0 improves debuggability when JWT signing or verification fails because an algorithm cannot be resolved. The library keeps the same public exception types for unsupported algorithms, but now preserves the original lookup failure as the exception cause.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that JWT signing and verification failures caused by an unavailable or unsupported algorithm preserve the original cause while continuing to surface the existing public error types.

expectation.grounded: In PyJWS, when algorithm lookup fails during signing, the library should continue to raise NotImplementedError for unsupported algorithms, including the case where a cryptography-backed algorithm implementation cannot be found, and that exception should be chained from the originating KeyError. When algorithm lookup fails during verification, the library should continue to raise InvalidAlgorithmError and chain it from the originating KeyError.
expectation.conceptual: When a caller requests a JWT algorithm the library cannot resolve, the operation should still fail with the same high-level exception type as before, but the failure should retain its underlying cause so callers and debugging tools can trace why the algorithm was unavailable.

constraints.grounded: Do not change the public exception classes raised for these conditions: signing failures from unresolved algorithms must remain NotImplementedError, and verification failures from unresolved algorithms must remain InvalidAlgorithmError. Successful signing, successful verification, and signature mismatch handling must remain unchanged.
constraints.conceptual: This upgrade should improve diagnostics only. It must not alter normal JWT behavior, supported success paths, or the category of user-visible error raised for unsupported algorithms.

behavior: When signing with an algorithm that is not present in the library's algorithm registry, the library raises NotImplementedError and preserves the underlying lookup failure as the exception cause.

When signing with an algorithm that depends on cryptography and the implementation cannot be found, the library raises NotImplementedError and preserves the underlying lookup failure as the exception cause.

When verifying a token with an algorithm that is not present in the library's algorithm registry, the library raises InvalidAlgorithmError and preserves the underlying lookup failure as the exception cause.
acceptance_criteria: When an application signs a JWT using an unsupported algorithm, it should receive a NotImplementedError whose cause reflects the underlying algorithm lookup failure.

When an application signs a JWT using an algorithm that requires cryptography but no implementation can be resolved, it should receive a NotImplementedError whose cause reflects the underlying algorithm lookup failure.
When an application verifies a JWT using an unsupported algorithm, it should receive an InvalidAlgorithmError whose cause reflects the underlying algorithm lookup failure.
When an application signs or verifies JWTs with supported algorithms, the upgrade should not change successful behavior or signature validation outcomes.

task_1.title: Restore backward-compatible JWT decode kwargs
task_1.description: PyJWT 2.3.0 restores backward compatibility in the JWT decode APIs by accepting arbitrary keyword arguments again. Recognized validation kwargs such as audience, issuer, and leeway continue to affect claim validation, while additional unused kwargs no longer fail at call time purely because of the function signature.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that JWT decoding remains backward compatible when callers pass validation-related keyword arguments or extra keyword arguments, so upgrading to 2.3.0 does not break existing decode call sites.

expectation.grounded: The public decode APIs, including `jwt.decode` and `jwt.decode_complete`, should accept arbitrary keyword arguments again. Supported kwargs used by claim validation, including `audience`, `issuer`, and `leeway`, must still be honored during payload validation, and additional unrecognized kwargs must not trigger argument-binding failures while decoding. Forwarding through the JWS decode layer must also tolerate these kwargs.
expectation.conceptual: Decoding a token should keep working for applications that pass validation options as keyword arguments, and the upgrade should stop rejecting calls simply because they include extra unused keyword parameters.

constraints.grounded: Restoring keyword-argument compatibility must not change normal signature verification, payload decoding, option merging, or existing claim-validation outcomes for supported parameters. Invalid tokens and invalid supported validation inputs should continue to surface the library's normal decode or claim-validation errors.
constraints.conceptual: This compatibility fix must not weaken token validation or change successful decode results beyond allowing previously rejected keyword-argument call patterns.

behavior: `jwt.decode` and `jwt.decode_complete` accept arbitrary keyword arguments in addition to their core parameters.
Keyword arguments for claim validation, including `audience`, `issuer`, and `leeway`, continue to control payload claim checks during decode.
Extra keyword arguments that are not used by decode-time validation are tolerated instead of causing a function-signature error.
Keyword arguments can be forwarded through the JWS decode path without breaking signature verification or payload extraction.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller passes `audience`, `issuer`, or `leeway` as keyword arguments to `jwt.decode` or `jwt.decode_complete`, decoding should proceed and apply the corresponding claim validation.
When a caller passes additional unused keyword arguments to the decode APIs, the call should not fail solely because those keywords are present.
When decode is executed through the JWS layer with forwarded keyword arguments, signature verification and payload decoding should behave the same as before.

When a token fails claim validation for supported keyword arguments, or a supported validation argument is invalid, decoding should still raise the normal validation error rather than silently succeeding.
